notes:
Summary:
- Mid-market multi-tenant SaaS (customer engagement automation) exploring Redwood for hosted -> dedicated path.
- Primary evaluation: chat/agent workloads with strict streaming latency SLOs, tenant-level quotas and per-tenant rate limiting, stable tool-calling (external DB/function hooks).

Customer goals / KPIs:
- First-token streaming latency target: <= 120ms p50 for single-tenant happy path; p95 goal <= 250ms across 8 concurrent tenants.
- Per-tenant throughput: typical tenants 5-20 concurrent sessions; peak tenant burst up to 200 tpm.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market ARR profile, wants usage-based for Hosted during POC but likely reserved commit for Dedicated if steady.
- Multi-tenant isolation: strict quotaing per tenant, per-tenant billing metrics, bulk tenant onboarding automation.

Recent activity / timeline:
- 2025-02-18: Discovery call (Diego + Priya) — mapped high-level architecture; customer provided traffic profile spreadsheet. (ff_20250218_discovery)
- 2025-02-25: Product demo focused on streaming + tool-calling; showed function call patterns and fallback policies. CTO quote: "Stream must be reliable — first token <120ms or we fail UX." (ff_20250225_demo_streaming)
- 2025-02-27: Send POC scope doc and test harness template (drive link).
- 2025-03-01: Security intake request: want SOC2 type II report + SAML plan; asked about KMS and audit log retention. Logged REDW-874 for streaming stability questions.
- 2025-03-04: Pricing intro call; customer asked for Dedicated breakpoints and commitment tradeoffs; procurement asked for SLA language.

POC scope (agreed tentative):
- 2-week Hosted API POC validating streaming latency and tool-calling flow against synthetic load (3 tenant profiles: small/med/large).
- Metrics to capture: first-byte latency, end-to-end tool-call latency, per-tenant error rate, token cost per session, cold-start behavior.
- Failure scenarios: fallback to smaller model variant, rate-limit enforcement, graceful degradation when KV cache miss spikes.
- Success criteria: p50 first-token <=120ms and p95 <=250ms for med tenant under 50 concurrent sessions, stable streaming (no >1% frame drop), correct tool-call integrity "always" on 99% of runs.

Architecture & product asks from SE side:
- Need recommended batching/windowing config for conversation workloads across multi-tenant pools.
- Ask for sample routing policy: route to lower-cost variant outside business hours; automatic fallback to cached responses for common prompts.
- Require per-tenant rate limit controls and quota APIs (create/update/usage endpoints) + tenant-level tracing in Console.

Pricing / commercial notes:
- Prefers posted Hosted API for POC; wants clear math on token cost vs Dedicated reservation.
- Potential ARR band if move to Dedicated: $75k-$180k / year.
- Procurement wants SLA and data residency clause before committing.

Open questions & blockers:
- Can Redwood guarantee streaming stability for multi-tenant eviction scenarios? (SE to propose isolation knobs).
- How are per-tenant quotas surfaced in Console and via API? Need demo.
- SOC2 evidence timing and whether Private (VPC) required for any customers in their vertical.

Next steps (short):
- SE (Priya) to deliver architecture deep-dive + batching recommendations (target 2025-03-10).
- Sales (Diego) to share Dedicated pricing sheet and sample SLA language by 2025-03-07.
- Security to share SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration notes; customer to confirm retention/residency requirements.
- Schedule POC kickoff after security signoff (target wk of 2025-03-17).

Notes style: shorthand, bullets, some direct quotes from CTO. Attachments: drive://redwood/shared/pricing/mynerva-dedicated-quote-v1.pdf; jira REDW-874 for streaming flakiness.
